courses.name: Introduction to Programming and Computational Problem-Solving: Accelerated Pace
courses.description: Introduces Java programming at an accelerated pace, from control flow and data structures through class design, recursion, events and files.
courses.prerequisites: restricted to undergraduates. Graduate students will be allowed as space permits.

category_review.locator: CSE 11. Introduction to Programming and Computational Problem-Solving: Accelerated Pace (4)
category_review.rationale: Programming constructs and object-oriented design are the central learning content.

courses.name: Basic Data Structures and Object-Oriented Design
courses.description: Implements data structures and object-oriented design using Java, including recursion and abstract data types.
courses.prerequisites: CSE 8B or CSE 11; restricted to undergraduates. Graduate students will be allowed as space permits.

category_review.locator: CSE 12 Basic Data Structures and Object-Oriented Design
category_review.rationale: The official description centers on data structures, object-oriented design and recursion.

courses.name: Software Tools and Techniques Laboratory
courses.description: Practices development tools, systematic debugging and software laboratory documentation.
courses.prerequisites: CSE 8B or CSE 11 or CSE 12 or DSC 30; restricted to undergraduates. Graduate students will be allowed as space permits.

category_review.locator: CSE 15L. Software Tools and Techniques Laboratory (2)
category_review.rationale: Software construction and debugging methods establish foundational programming practice.

courses.name: Systems Programming and Software Tools
courses.description: Studies program execution, storage and communication through C programs and Unix development tools.
courses.prerequisites: CSE 11 or CSE 8B or ECE 15; two units of credit offered for CSE 29 if CSE 15L taken previously.

category_review.locator: CSE 29. Systems Programming and Software Tools (4)
category_review.rationale: The stated organizing concern is how computers execute programs; systems programming supports that study.

courses.name: Discrete Mathematics
courses.description: Uses logic, sets, relations and proof techniques to reason about computing problems.
courses.prerequisites: CSE 11 or CSE 6R or CSE 8A or CSE 8B or ECE 15. Prerequisite courses must have been completed with a grade of C– or better; restricted to undergraduates. Graduate students will be allowed as space permits.

category_review.rationale: Logic and proof methods, rather than programming, organize the course.

category_review.locator: CSE 21. Mathematics for Algorithms and Systems (4)
category_review.rationale: Discrete mathematical modeling and analysis are the explicit content.

courses.name: Computer Organization
courses.description: Studies assembly programming, digital logic, processor design and performance, and memory organization.
courses.prerequisites: CSE 15L or CSE 29 or ECE 15; restricted to undergraduates. Graduate students will be allowed as space permits.

category_review.rationale: The official description centers on processor organization, digital logic, assembly and memory hierarchy.

courses.name: Fluency in Information Technology
courses.description: Builds practical familiarity with information technology, computers and networks.
courses.prerequisites: none.

category_review.rationale: Basic digital fluency does not establish programming foundations or systems architecture depth.

courses.name: Mathematical Beauty in Rome
courses.description: Analyzes Roman architectural structures using geometry, engineering concepts and computer models.
courses.prerequisites: MATH 10A or MATH 20A; department approval, and corequisite of CSE 6GS.

category_review.rationale: The description combines geometric analysis with a specific architectural application.

courses.name: Introduction to Computer Science and Object-Oriented Programming: Python
courses.description: Introduces Python programming, data structures, recursion, algorithm complexity and object-oriented design.

category_review.locator: CSE 6R. Introduction to Computer Science and Object-Oriented Programming: Python (4)
category_review.rationale: Programming concepts and computational problem solving are the substantive content.

courses.name: Mathematical Beauty in Rome Lab
courses.description: Applies the companion architecture course through field experiments and detailed computer models of Roman structures.
courses.prerequisites: MATH 10A or MATH 20A; department approval, and corequisite of CSE 4GS.

category_review.locator: CSE 6GS. Mathematical Beauty in Rome Lab (4)
category_review.rationale: Architectural modeling applies the companion geometric and engineering theory.

courses.name: Introduction to Programming and Computational Problem-Solving I
courses.description: Introduces programming constructs, structured data and the process of designing, executing and debugging programs.
courses.prerequisites: restricted to undergraduates. Graduate students will be allowed as space permits.

category_review.locator: CSE 8A. Introduction to Programming and Computational Problem-Solving I (4)
category_review.rationale: The explicit focus is introductory programming practice.

courses.name: Building and Programming Electronic Devices
courses.description: Uses team projects to program Arduino devices and design a working physical artifact.
courses.prerequisites: restricted to first-year and sophomore students; instructor approval required.

category_review.locator: CSE 42. Building and Programming Electronic Devices (2)
category_review.rationale: The course combines programming practice with physical device applications.

courses.name: C++ for Java Programmers
courses.description: Extends Java programmers' skills to C++ pointers, templates, libraries and runtime behavior.
courses.prerequisites: CSE 12 or consent of instructor.

category_review.rationale: Programming-language knowledge and implementation practice are central.

courses.name: Introduction to Computer Science and Engineering Seminar
courses.description: Introduces CSE resources and relationships among computing topics through faculty-led seminars.
courses.prerequisites: Restricted to students in the CSE-PACE program. Prerequisites: none.

category_review.locator: CSE 89. Introduction to Computer Science and Engineering Seminar (2)
category_review.rationale: The general orientation description does not establish a single subject category.

courses.name: Undergraduate Seminar
courses.description: Presents an instructor-selected current computing research topic in a seminar.

category_review.rationale: The changing topic is unspecified; a computing prefix does not identify its subject.

courses.name: Perspectives in Computer Science and Engineering
courses.description: Discusses relationships, developments and future directions across computing topics.
courses.prerequisites: majors only.

category_review.locator: CSE 91. Perspectives in Computer Science and Engineering (2)
category_review.rationale: The broad seminar description does not identify a stable specific subject.

courses.name: Tutor Apprenticeship
courses.description: Trains new CSE tutors through individual and group mentoring in effective tutoring.
courses.prerequisites: Concurrent tutor appointment in a CSE course is required.

category_review.rationale: The described activity is teaching practice rather than a particular computing subject.

courses.name: Independent Study in Computer Science and Engineering
courses.description: Supports faculty-supervised independent reading or research by special arrangement.
courses.prerequisites: lower-division standing. Completion of thirty units at UC San Diego with a UC San Diego GPA of 3.0. Special Studies form required. Department stamp required. Consent of instructor and approval of the department.

category_review.locator: CSE 99. Independent Study in Computer Science and Engineering (4)
category_review.rationale: The research subject is not specified and cannot be classified from the course number.

courses.name: Biology Meets Computing
courses.description: Introduces Python while solving biological problems with bioinformatics tools.
courses.prerequisites: BILD 1 or BILD 4 or CSE 11 or CSE 3 or CSE 8A or CSE 8B.

category_review.rationale: The description explicitly combines learning programming and applying it to biology.

courses.name: Biology Meets Computing
courses.description: Introduces Python and biological problem solving through a fully online bioinformatics course.
courses.prerequisites: BILD 1 or BILD 4 or CSE 11 or CSE 3 or CSE 8A or CSE 8B.

category_review.rationale: Both programming instruction and biological applications are explicit; online delivery does not change subject.

courses.name: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Introduces AI approaches, history, applications and ethical questions through applied projects.
courses.prerequisites: COGS 18 or CSE 11 or CSE 6R or CSE 8A or CSE 8B or DSC 20. Restricted to students within the CS29 major. All other students will be allowed as space permits. This course is intended for students with no prior AI or ML experience. This course is intended for students with no prior AI or ML experience. Students may receive credit for one of the following: CSE 5, CSE 5R, or CSE 25.

category_review.rationale: The official description introduces AI approaches with application projects; ethics is a supporting component.

courses.name: Foundations of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
courses.description: Builds mathematical and programming foundations for AI, including optimization and representation learning.
courses.prerequisites: CSE 12 and CSE 25 and CSE 15L or CSE 29 and MATH 18 or MATH 31AH and MATH 20C or MATH 31BH; restricted to students within the CS29 major. All other students will be allowed as space permits.

category_review.locator: CSE 55 Foundations of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
category_review.rationale: The official description applies optimization and linear algebra to machine learning and representation learning; the explicit ML methodological focus supports AI classification.

courses.name: Calculus for Science and Engineering
courses.description: Differential and introductory integral calculus of one variable.
courses.prerequisites: Math Placement Exam qualifying score, or AP Precalculus score of 5, or AP Calculus AB score of 3 (or equivalent AB subscore on BC exam), or MATH 4C or MATH 10A.

category_review.rationale: The official description centers on one-variable calculus and its mathematical methods.

courses.name: Calculus for Science and Engineering
courses.description: Integral calculus, infinite series and polar coordinates.
courses.prerequisites: AP Calculus AB score of 4 or 5, or AP Calculus BC score of 3, or MATH 20A with a grade of C– or better, or MATH 10B with a grade of C– or better, or MATH 10C with a grade of C– or better.

category_review.rationale: The official description centers on one-variable calculus and its mathematical methods.

courses.prerequisites: MATH 20B and CSE 21 or MATH 154 or MATH 158 or MATH 184 or MATH 188; restricted to CS25, CS26, CS27, CS28, and CS29 majors. Other students will be allowed as space permits.

category_review.locator: CSE 103. A Practical Introduction to Probability and Statistics (4)
category_review.rationale: Probability and statistical theory are the main content despite one machine-learning application.

courses.description: Studies implementation and performance of advanced data structures.
courses.prerequisites: CSE 21 or MATH 154 or MATH 158 or MATH 184 or MATH 188 and CSE 12 and CSE 15L or CSE 29 or ECE 15; restricted to undergraduates. requirements.title: CSE elective eligibility

requirements.title: Topics-course limit
requirements.summary: CSE 190 and graduate analogue CSE 291 share a maximum of twelve units / three distinct topics.

requirements.title: P/NP and special studies
requirements.summary: At most twelve P/NP units: up to eight in CSE 198/199/199H, four in CSE 197, and two in CSE 109. Exceeding the special-studies limit requires faculty-reviewed petition.

requirements.title: Global Ties limit
requirements.summary: Up to eight ENG 100D/L units within the special-studies maximum; ENG 100D may count only once.

requirements.title: Letter grades
requirements.summary: All courses require letter grades except courses offered only P/NP.

requirements.title: Graduate degree reuse
requirements.summary: Graduate coursework counted in the undergraduate degree cannot also count in a graduate degree.

requirements.title: University degree minimums
requirements.summary: Complete at least 180 quarter units, including 60 upper-division units, an approved major, and the enrolled college’s requirements. These degree totals include the major; they are not added to its 124 units.

requirements.title: Senior residence
requirements.summary: Complete 35 of the final 45 units in residence in the degree-awarding UC college/school. Provost exceptions may cover approved UC visitors, Education Abroad, UCDC or UC Sacramento. UCSD Extension concurrent enrollment does not qualify. Roosevelt publishes a different 36/44 rule, retained separately.

requirements.title: Diversity, equity and inclusion
requirements.summary: Pass one approved four-unit course at C− or P or better; an articulated equivalent transfer course can qualify. Applies to lower-division entrants from Fall 2011 and upper-division entrants from Fall 2013. Approved finite course pool remains unreviewed.

requirements.title: American History and Institutions alternatives
requirements.summary: Qualify through C or better high-school US history (one unit, or half history plus half civics/government), an approved UCSD course at C−/P, AP US history/government at least 3, IB higher History of Americas at least 5, the page’s historical SAT II threshold 550, prior accepted California-college satisfaction, or acceptable college history/government at C or better. F-1/J-1 temporary residents may petition the college provost. Approved course pool remains unreviewed.

requirements.title: Entry writing placement and completion
requirements.summary: Complete placement before enrollment if entry writing is unsatisfied. College-writing placement satisfies the requirement. AWP 3 allows three consecutive quarters; AWP 4A allows three, then 4B follows immediately. Failure of the 4B portfolio leads to AWP 3, with at most three more consecutive quarters or five total. Earn C or better in AWP 3 or 4B before college writing. External UC entry-qualification alternatives remain to be inventoried.

requirements.title: Completion-time limits from Fall 2019
requirements.summary: First-year entrants have twelve quarters and transfers six. Beyond the limit, an approved college completion plan is required. Summer, approved part-time quarters, and quarters withdrawn from all courses do not count. Earlier-entry unit-limit rules are distinct.

requirements.title: Graduation application
requirements.summary: File the degree/diploma application with the college by its deadline; late filing needs special approval. Finish all coursework by the filed quarter’s end, otherwise submit a new application.

requirements.title: Double-major approvals and unique work
requirements.summary: Good-standing students need both departments and the college provost to approve. Each major needs at least ten unique upper-division courses (40 units); lower-division overlap is unrestricted. Two Engineering majors are not allowed, nor ordinarily two within one department. Additional major-specific prohibitions must also be checked.

requirements.title: Continuing-student protection
requirements.summary: Requirement changes should not substantially obstruct continuing students. Colleges/departments may deny this protection after an interruption longer than two years; no automatic mapping of the tentative 2026 AI plan onto earlier entrants.

requirements.title: 2026–27 direct-admit restriction
requirements.summary: The dated tentative department page admits only students directly placed in AI by Admissions in 2026–27. Internal switches and selective-major entry into AI are unavailable. AI students may leave for another CSE major but cannot switch back under this policy; review is planned in 2027, without a guarantee of changed eligibility.

requirements.title: Department grade and overlap policy
requirements.summary: The department requires C− or better and letter grading for major work except its specified P/NP-only exceptions (CSE 89, 91, 95, 109, 197, 198, 199). Each course serves only one core, AI elective, breadth or open-elective requirement. Graduate enrollment needs instructor and departmental TEA approval; similar undergraduate/graduate credit may require petition. Tentative-page course eligibility differences remain explicit.

requirements.title: Revelle College pathway (only if enrolled here)
requirements.summary: For first-year entrants: five-course humanities sequence; one fine arts; two social sciences; three mathematics including calculus; five sciences including biology, chemistry and physics; and fourth-quarter language proficiency or approved exam/native-language route. IGETC transfers retain mathematics, science and HUM 100; from Fall 2024 transfers need HUM 100, and transfers without UC reciprocity need four sciences. UC reciprocity exempts lower-division GE. Finite lists remain unreviewed.

requirements.title: John Muir College pathway (only if enrolled here)
requirements.summary: Complete four approved three-course sequences: social science; mathematics or natural science; and two of fine arts, humanities and languages (48 units). At most three major courses overlap GE. Complete letter-graded MCWP 40 and 50 (8 units), without AP/IB substitution. IGETC or UC-reciprocity transfers may waive GE sequences; IGETC transfers still take MCWP 125 or request MCWP 50. Finite sequence lists remain unreviewed.

requirements.title: Thurgood Marshall College pathway (only if enrolled here)
requirements.summary: First-year GE: three-course Dimensions of Culture at UCSD for letter grades; one nonperformance fine art; biology, chemistry and physics; two mathematics/statistics/logic courses in the stated allowable combinations; two approved humanities/cultural studies; and four courses outside the major, including two upper-division and at least one upper-division writing course. Optional four-unit public service may replace one breadth and meet writing. Transfers retain one approved upper-division writing and one noncontiguous upper-division breadth course, with additional needs determined from credit. Approved lists remain unreviewed.

requirements.title: Earl Warren College pathway (only if enrolled here)
requirements.summary: Complete letter-graded WCWP 10A–B and the two Ethics and Society choices PHIL/POLI 27 and 28; two approved formal-skills courses. BS Engineering students complete two three-course area studies outside the major, one humanities/fine arts and one social sciences, each with at least two upper-division courses. Interdisciplinary studies require college approval; a minor may substitute. AP/IB may supply at most four units per area study. Certified transfers take WCWP 100 plus one upper-division course outside the major; other transfers take WCWP 100 and area studies. AI-specific engineering area-study applicability and finite pools need confirmation.

requirements.title: Eleanor Roosevelt College pathway (only if enrolled here)
requirements.summary: First-year GE: five MMW courses; two natural sciences; two quantitative methods; language through fourth quarter or proficiency; one four-unit fine art; three courses in one geographic region including two upper-division; and qualifying upper-division written work graded C− or better. Transfer pathways use MMW 121/121R/122 with additional language/GE conditions based on certification; unmet first-year writing adds MMW 12/13. The college prints residence 36 of final 44 units, unlike university 35/45. Approved pools and full transfer conditions remain unresolved.

requirements.title: Sixth College pathway (only if enrolled here)
requirements.summary: Complete CAT 1–3; one information-technology fluency; seven inquiry courses (two social sciences, two humanities, two natural sciences, one math/logic); one statistics; two art-making; four-unit upper-division experiential learning; and four-unit upper-division CAT 125 or 125R. Transfer agreements may meet some lower-division requirements; approved pools and exact transfer applicability remain unreviewed.

requirements.title: Seventh College pathway (only if enrolled here)
requirements.summary: Complete SYN 1/1R, SYN 2/2R and SYN 100; two approved courses each in arts, humanities, natural sciences/engineering, quantitative reasoning and social sciences; and one 2–4 unit high-impact experience. Alternatives/high-impact may overlap major, minor and university requirements. All transfers retain SYN 100 and high-impact; recommended SYN 150 can satisfy high-impact if letter graded. Approved pools and additional transfer needs remain unreviewed.

requirements.title: Eighth College pathway (only if enrolled here)
requirements.summary: Complete CCE 1, 2, 3 and 120, plus two approved courses each in arts, humanities, natural sciences, quantitative methods/engineering and social sciences. Breadth may overlap major, minor and university requirements. Certified transfers retain CCE 110 and 120; others receive individual credit evaluation. CCE courses require letter grades. The catalog explicitly lists the climate-change requirement for Fall 2024 and later admits; its approved pool remains unreviewed.

requirements.title: Systems CSE course tags
requirements.summary: Observed tags in course headings. A course already used for core, AI electives or another breadth requirement cannot count again; CSE 190 topics require offering-specific review.

requirements.title: Theory/Abstraction CSE course tags
requirements.summary: Observed tags in course headings. A course already used for core, AI electives or another breadth requirement cannot count again; CSE 190 topics require offering-specific review.

requirements.title: Applications of Computing CSE course tags
requirements.summary: Observed tags in course headings. A course already used for core, AI electives or another breadth requirement cannot count again; CSE 190 topics require offering-specific review.

requirements.title: UC entry-writing test alternatives
requirements.summary: Qualify through AP English Language/Literature, Seminar or Research at least 3; IB English LanguageA higher level at least 5 or standard level at least 6; ACT ELA at least 30 or combined English+Reading at least 63 from one sitting; or pre-March 2024 paper SAT reading/writing at least 680. Digital SAT and ACT English alone do not satisfy ELWR. Official test scores are due July 15; these placement uses do not imply admission-test use.

requirements.title: UC entry-writing pre-enrollment course alternative
requirements.summary: Before UC enrollment, earn C or better in a UC-transferable composition course worth 3 semester or 4 quarter units at an institution accredited by a former regional accreditor. Otherwise follow the campus placement/completion route; UCSD’s specific AWP timeline remains separately represented.

requirements.title: Climate requirement applicability
requirements.summary: Regulation 600H applies to first-year/lower-division entrants from Fall 2024. Transfers are exempt. Pass one approved one-quarter course at C− or P or better; no four-unit minimum is inferred from the DEI rule.

requirements.title: Distance-education unit ceiling
requirements.summary: Regulation 600B4, enacted June 3, 2025, prohibits 50 percent or more of UCSD-earned units from designated distance courses unless the major is approved as a distance-education program. No AI exemption is presumed.

requirements.title: Residence and approved external-program exceptions
requirements.summary: Minimum UC residence is three terms; a summer course of at least 2 units can count as half a term. Normally 35 of final 45 units must be resident. Students completing all requirements in an approved EAP/UCDC/UC Sacramento/NRS ecology program may use the preceding 45 units; faculty may alternatively permit 35 of final 90, including final 12, resident units. Roosevelt’s 36/44 catalog discrepancy remains visible.

requirements.title: Climate course credit and overlap
requirements.summary: AP/IB does not satisfy the climate requirement, including AP-derived ESYS 10 credit. Approved courses may overlap GE, DEI, major or minor requirements. First-time first-year entrants from Fall 2024 are covered; earlier matriculants and incoming transfers are exempt. Term offering lists are scheduling information, not the complete approved pool.

requirements.title: American History and Institutions course options
requirements.summary: One listed course or a HIUS course other than a colloquium, at C− or P or better. The open HIUS predicate is source-stated; it does not require enumerating every changing HIUS offering. Other documented non-course routes remain alternatives.

requirements.title: DEI approved options with date restrictions
requirements.summary: Select one eligible approved option under its stated date, prerequisite and enrollment conditions. Historical expired and future approvals are retained for their stated periods, not asserted currently usable. Complex printed rows retain their unresolved internal notation.

requirements.title: Revelle transfer humanities route

requirements.title: Revelle mathematics equivalence, grading and placement
requirements.summary: Letter grading required. At most one of MATH 11, PSYC 60 and AP Statistics (score at least 3) counts. Fall-2024 rules apply to all admit types; older first-year entrants before Fall 2024 and transfers before Fall 2023 had two calculus courses plus one additional option and need advising to change their audit. Placement-test exemptions: AP Calculus AB/BC at least 2, IB Mathematics Analyses & Approaches HL at least 5, or prior college calculus at C− or better. Credit is not awarded below AP/IB placement. Former MATH 20F is an alias, not an extra current choice.

requirements.title: Revelle science cohort and discipline rules
requirements.summary: Conditional Revelle route. First-year entrants take five courses: one each in biology, chemistry and physics, plus two approved science options. Transfers from Fall 2026 take three: two different disciplines among biology/chemistry/physics, plus one approved option. Pre-Fall-2024 transfers follow five courses. This page does not resolve Fall 2024/2025 transfers; the separately cited catalog describes four courses. Do not merge these cohort rules.

requirements.title: Revelle science grading and laboratories
requirements.summary: Approved R versions count. Science/engineering/mathematics majors are advised to use letter grades unless their major does not require them. Revelle itself does not require labs; departmental rules still apply, and the listed PHYS 1 lecture/lab pairs require concurrent enrollment. Table subheadings advise different preparations/majors, not a separate AI-specific science pool.

requirements.title: Revelle language proficiency alternatives
requirements.summary: First-year entrants need fourth-quarter/third-semester proficiency; transfers need second-quarter/second-semester proficiency. Course endpoints below depend on entry type, not all preceding courses as universal requirements. P/NP is permitted. Alternatives include the college proficiency examination, qualifying AP/IB or SAT II (700), a qualifying heritage course, or non-English native language plus at least one year of high school abroad taught in another language, with transcript/advising review. Placement alone is not an award of course credit.

requirements.title: Muir first-year GE structure
requirements.summary: Conditional Muir route: writing sequence; three courses in one math/natural-science theme; three in one social-science theme; and three courses in each of two distinct areas chosen from fine arts, humanities and a single language. Each nonlanguage area uses one approved theme. Themes and areas below are alternatives, not all additional requirements. Nonwriting GE permits D or better or P. Prior AP/IB/transfer credit cannot be duplicated; enrollment prerequisites still apply; off-list petitions are possible but not guaranteed. Language needs college credit, not placement/proficiency exemption.

requirements.title: Muir writing sequence step 1
requirements.summary: Choose one listed variant at this sequence step; letter grade D or better.

requirements.title: Muir writing sequence step 2
requirements.summary: Choose one listed variant at this sequence step; letter grade D or better.

requirements.title: Muir GE overlap and writing sequence
requirements.summary: At most three major courses may count toward Muir GE in total. Complete writing in order at D or better with letter grading; AP/IB/community-college credit does not clear it. First-pass enrollment priority lasts through quarter six for the two-course writing route. Other GE allows D/P and applicable AP/IB/transfer credit.

requirements.title: Muir transfer-certification branches
requirements.summary: IGETC or CalGETC transfers take MCWP 125 or 125R at letter grade D or better, with first-pass priority through quarter three. Partial IGETC also requires the remaining one or two certified areas. Transfers who completed another campus’s GE take the two-course Muir writing sequence but may petition prior writing for partial/full fulfillment. Other transfers follow first-year requirements, with transcript review. The catalog’s possible MCWP 50 substitution is not repeated by this current page; no automatic substitution is assumed.

requirements.title: Warren engineering pathway explicitly includes AI
requirements.summary: The published B.S. Engineering list explicitly includes CSE Artificial Intelligence. For Warren first-year/noncertified transfer routes, choose one humanities/fine-arts and one social-science Area Study, both unrelated to AI and each other. Each has three four-unit courses, including two upper-division and at least one UCSD course. This resolves applicability; the six-course PofC route for nonengineering majors is not imposed on AI.

requirements.title: Area-study grades, overlap and discipline limits
requirements.summary: P/NP is permitted. Upper-division major/minor courses cannot overlap Area Study or other GE, apart from separately permitted major/minor overlap. No MGT courses; no language courses in social-science studies and at most two in humanities studies. A # subject may occupy only one discipline. Humanities and Perspectives of Social Science cannot be the two chosen studies. Special Studies 195 is excluded by the general GE page.

requirements.title: Optional noncontiguous minor substitution
requirements.summary: A qualifying minor may replace its discipline’s Area Study; interdisciplinary substitution requires at least four minor courses in that discipline and advising review. A business minor needs three approved upper-division social-science courses outside MGT. At most two applicable upper-division courses/eight units may overlap major and minor. These are optional approval predicates, not a requirement to complete every minor.

requirements.title: Humanities specialized selection rule
requirements.summary: Published eligible department predicates: History (HI**); Literature (LT**); Music (MUS); Philosophy (PHIL); Study of Religion (RELI); Theatre and Dance (TD**); Visual Arts (VIS). Any three four-unit courses, at least two upper division. Humanities excludes linguistics/language; it cannot pair with Perspectives of Social Science. Off-list applicable humanities courses may be petitioned before enrollment.

requirements.title: Human Developmental Sciences specialized selection rule
requirements.summary: Published eligible department predicates: Anthropology (ANTH); Communication (COMM); Human Development Sciences (HDS); Linguistics (LIGN); Psychology (PSYC); Sociology (SOCI); Urban Studies and Development (USP). Take HDS 1 and two upper-division courses in Human Developmental Sciences from those departments; not every course in each department is automatically eligible.

requirements.title: Perspectives of Social Science specialized selection rule
requirements.summary: Published eligible department predicates: Anthropology (ANTH); Communication (COMM); Economics (ECON); Education Sciences (EDS); Ethnic Studies (ETHN); Human Developmental Sciences (HDS); Linguistic/General (LIGN); Political Science (POLI); Psychology (PSYC); Sociology (SOCI); Urban Studies and Planning (USP). Any three four-unit courses, at least two upper division; cannot pair with Humanities. This area study does not itself satisfy minor requirements.

requirements.title: Law-and-society topical and date restrictions
requirements.summary: ANSC 100, HIUS 181 and SOCI 120T need a law-related topic and prior Warren approval. The page’s asterisk excludes designated courses taken before Winter 2022; ** denotes cross-listing. The embedded table prints ETHN 153*** without a matching triple-asterisk explanation, retained as unresolved.

requirements.title: Warren certified-transfer noncontiguous route
requirements.summary: For the certified-transfer GE branch: one four-unit upper-division course outside the major’s discipline, taken at UCSD, UCEAP or another UC campus. P/NP permitted. No major overlap except noncontiguous double majors; an appropriate upper-division minor course may substitute. One noncontiguous Special Studies 197/198/199 may qualify. MGT does not qualify; environmental studies/FMPH needs advising. Prerequisites still apply.

requirements.title: Humanities and Fine Arts transfer predicates
requirements.summary: Approved departments: Chinese Studies; Classical Studies; Global South Studies; History; Japanese Studies; Jewish Studies; Linguistics (Heritage Language Only); Literature; Music; Philosophy; Study of Religion; Theatre and Dance; Visual Arts. Choose outside the major discipline; these are department predicates, not a finite universal course list.

requirements.title: Math, Natural Sciences, Physical Sciences and Engineering transfer predicates
requirements.summary: Approved departments: Biology; Chemistry; Cognitive Science; Environmental Systems; Mathematics; Physics; Scripps Institution of Oceanography. Choose outside the major discipline; these are department predicates, not a finite universal course list.

requirements.title: Social Sciences transfer predicates

requirements.title: Marshall first-year sequence and distributions
requirements.summary: DOC 1/2/3 must be letter graded and completed at UCSD, normally within two years. ELWR precedes DOC 2/3. Science: one each biology, chemistry and physics. Mathematics/statistics/logic: either two advanced-math/statistics, one advanced plus one introductory-statistics/programming-logic, or one introductory statistics plus one programming-logic. Humanities/cultural studies: two; fine arts: one. Approved science/math courses may overlap the major.

requirements.title: Marshall disciplinary breadth distribution
requirements.summary: Four four-unit courses outside the major discipline, including two upper division and at least one approved significant-writing course. No major overlap. Noncontiguous double majors need one upper-division writing breadth course, from any discipline but not counted in either major. Public-service coursework is an approved route subject to its program rules.

requirements.title: Marshall MUS 80 eligibility
requirements.summary: MUS 80 must be taken for four units to count as fine arts; the requirement does not establish every listed course’s credit value.

requirements.title: Marshall certified-transfer and partial-certification routes
requirements.summary: IGETC/CalGETC and UC Reciprocity waive lower-division GE; partial IGETC leaves one or two missing requirements at D or P, with advising for missing language. Two upper-division 100–199 courses of at least four units outside the major remain, including writing breadth. Transfer agreements do not apply to first-year admits.

requirements.title: Marshall Fall-2026 transfer writing rule
requirements.summary: For transfers admitted Fall 2026 onward, DOC 170 is the writing-breadth course, first available Winter 2027; it is part of the two-course upper-division breadth requirement, not an extra third course. The general writing list remains relevant to other eligible cohorts.

requirements.title: Marshall transfers without an agreement
requirements.summary: Prior completed lower-division GE at a non-UC four-year or out-of-state two-year institution can waive lower GE after a Letter of GE Completion and advising. Otherwise advising reviews each transfer course and determines remaining DOC, math, science, humanities, arts and up-to-four breadth requirements; petitions may be needed. This is an individual approval route, not an unprovided universal course list.

requirements.title: Marshall 2026–27 significant-writing eligibility
requirements.summary: List updated July 28, 2026. Qualifying English writing is completed outside class, discipline-appropriate and evaluated for writing as well as content: at least ten pages or two five-page papers. Exams do not count. The course must be outside the major discipline. Transfers from Fall 2026 must instead use DOC 170, available from Winter 2027. Summer 2026 requires the prior-year list from advising.

requirements.title: Sixth study-abroad proposal criteria
requirements.summary: Nonautomatic study-abroad work needs faculty supervision, at least four upper-division UC-transferable units appearing on the UCSD transcript, a passing grade and at least four in-person weeks; virtual exchanges do not qualify. Lower-division-only plans need special consideration. Do not reuse the course for another Sixth GE. Submit the Navigating Reentry activities worksheet and completion certificate by Friday of week eight in the quarter after return; decision by week ten. Proposals must be original student writing; AI-generated submissions are disallowed.

requirements.title: Sixth off-list UCSD course proposal
requirements.summary: Faculty-supervised upper-division work of at least four units must have substantial sustained experiential activity in a fulfillment track, active independent work, reflection and a final deliverable. These criteria are necessary but approval is not guaranteed. Supply the syllabus by Friday of week eight in the preceding quarter; decision by week ten. From Fall 2026, all four-unit 198/199 courses qualify automatically and need no proposal.

requirements.title: Explicit one-unit experiential alternative
requirements.summary: Passing fall-only CAT 90 fulfills experiential learning despite the ordinary four-upper-division-unit route. It is one unit, P/NP only, available at either class standing after an approved summer activity of at least 80 hours across five weeks, ending July 1–October 1 and not continuing in fall. No other academic credit for the activity. Obtain preauthorization and eligibility review; submit supervisor confirmation by end of week one. Paid, unpaid and co-curricular-record activities may qualify; failure leaves the requirement incomplete.

requirements.title: Sixth upper-division writing alternatives
requirements.summary: One CAT 125, online CAT 125R, or the explicitly allowed Global Seminar CAT 125GS variant meets writing. CAT 125/125R require completed lower-division writing and upper-division standing. No automatic permission to reuse one GS course for experiential learning and another Sixth GE is inferred.

requirements.title: Sixth published AP breadth alternatives
requirements.summary: IT: AP Computer Science A 4/5. Social Analysis: Economics, Government or Psychology 4/5. Humanities: African American Studies, Art History, History, non-English Language/Literature 3/4/5. Science: Biology, Chemistry or Physics 1/2/C 3/4/5, or Environmental Science 4/5. Math: Calculus AB/BC 3/4/5. Statistics: Statistics 3/4/5. Art Making: Art Studio or Music 3/4/5. “Can be used towards” an area is not assumed to satisfy its entire multi-course/unit requirement.

requirements.title: ERC first-year component rules
requirements.summary: First-year route: MMW 11–15, two quantitative/formal-skills courses, two natural sciences, fourth-quarter/third-semester language proficiency, one fine-art course of at least four units, three same-region courses including two upper division, and upper-division writing. MMW is letter graded at UCSD with no AP/IB/transfer substitution; ELWR precedes MMW 12/13 but does not waive 11. Approved R variants count. Quantitative, science and fine-arts P/NP options remain subject to major grading rules.

requirements.title: ERC overlap restrictions
requirements.summary: Lower-division major and all minor courses may overlap GE. Upper-division major courses cannot overlap ERC GE except writing; noncontiguous double majors may overlap at most three upper-division courses with GE. No GE-to-GE overlap except upper-division writing. Fine arts and regional specialization cannot overlap; language, including prerequisites to the endpoint, cannot overlap regional specialization. Up to two upper-division major/minor courses need department approval; no upper-division course may count in two minors.

requirements.title: ERC off-list upper-division writing petition
requirements.summary: Provide a syllabus and original English graded writing: either one paper of at least 2,500 words, or a portfolio totaling at least 3,000 words including one paper of at least 1,500. Work must earn C− or better and develop an evidence-supported original argument. Poetry, fiction, in-class exams, group work and lab reports do not qualify. This open petition route is not a missing finite list.

requirements.title: ERC language qualification
requirements.summary: Proficiency is fourth-quarter/third-semester level, placement into the fifth quarter at UCSD, or an approved UCSD proficiency exam. P/NP and approved R variants count. Self-directed LIGN 19 is excluded. SAT II Language at least 700 or eligible high school abroad may qualify after official scores/transcripts and advising review. The listed heritage LIHL route requires prior exposure, upper-division standing and Linguistics approval. A LIxx 1D/DX endpoint meets proficiency but later continuation/study abroad still requires LTxx 2A. AP/IB routes follow the separate credit chart.

requirements.title: ERC certified-transfer writing route
requirements.summary: Current page: complete certified IGETC, UC reciprocity or CalGETC before transfer, document it, and take MMW 122 at letter grade D or better. CalGETC without optional LOTE certification additionally needs one college LOTE course or approved proficiency. Transfer agreements are unavailable to first-year admits. This current single-course route differs from the separately retained catalog transfer sequence; applicability is not silently reconciled.

requirements.title: ERC partial and other transfer branches
requirements.summary: Partial IGETC or reciprocity leaves at most two certified missing areas, reviewed by advising. Use MMW 122 (4 units) after both IGETC 1A/1B or two semesters of writing, otherwise MMW 12 (6 units) after one; letter grade D or better. Prior complete/partial GE at another four-year institution needs a letter and the same writing-dependent MMW route. Without qualifying documentation use the general-transfer branch. General transfers complete remaining GE individually, including two upper-division same-region courses if needed; MMW 122 also satisfies writing. Current transfer table elsewhere says MMW121 or122, another visible inconsistency.

requirements.title: ERC component annotations and grading limits
requirements.summary: CSE 8A has a fall CSE-major restriction; math # entries are calculus preparation; ‡ statistics options are discouraged in the first quarter, not prohibited. ASTR 1–4 apply from Fall 2024 and their listed PHYS predecessors ended Spring 2024. PHYS 1 lecture/lab pairs require both; CENG/NANO 15/R variants allow credit only once. Fine arts permits four-unit MUS/TD/VIS courses numbered 1–199 plus listed exceptions, not one-to-three-unit classes. COMM 80 is for Speech and Debate Team members.

requirements.title: Current ERC degree/progress/residence policy
requirements.summary: Current public college page agrees with the Senate: 180 total/60 upper-division units, cumulative and major GPA at least 2.0, and 35 of final 45 units at UCSD. Its catalog still prints 36/44; this is retained as a source discrepancy. Minimum progress is 36 degree-applicable units per academic year. MMW 15 supplies first-year climate credit and must be letter graded. Students cannot individually petition an off-list DEI course; departments seek Senate approval. File the DDA from registration opening through final-exam week for the graduating quarter; ordinary first-year/transfer quarter limits and approved extensions apply.

requirements.title: ERC approved upper-division writing options
requirements.summary: Current-linked page is explicitly dated December 3, 2020. One approved English writing course at upper-division 100–199 level; R variants permitted. May overlap other requirements; MMW 121/122 are transfer-only and letter graded. * marks regional-or-fine-art eligibility, not both; ~ indicates possible regional overlap within the selected region. Other eligible work may be petitioned using the current GE-page criteria.

requirements.title: Multiculturalism in North America regional choices
requirements.summary: Select one region. First-year entrants take three courses including two upper division; transfers take two upper division. At most one course may be P/NP; AP counts as the lower-division slot, not the P/NP slot. Upper-division major overlap is prohibited; language and fine-arts requirements cannot reuse these courses. Approved upper-division writing overlap is allowed. This region is for Fall-2021-onward entrants; the earlier combined Americas region is not substituted. The page also permits the open predicate of courses on the DEI approved list, under regional distribution rules. Source updated August 2026. ^ marks the upper-division distribution reminder, # native-language instruction, * regional-or-fine-arts but not both, and ! possible DEI overlap subject to separate current approval evidence.

requirements.summary: Select one region. First-year entrants take three courses including two upper division; transfers take two upper division. At most one course may be P/NP; AP counts as the lower-division slot, not the P/NP slot. Upper-division major overlap is prohibited; language and fine-arts requirements cannot reuse these courses. Approved upper-division writing overlap is allowed. This region is for Fall-2021-onward entrants; the earlier combined Americas region is not substituted. Source updated August 2026. ^ marks the upper-division distribution reminder, # native-language instruction, * regional-or-fine-arts but not both, and ! possible DEI overlap subject to separate current approval evidence.

requirements.title: Eighth first-year CCE sequence
requirements.summary: CCE 1, 2, 3 and 120 are the four-course first-year sequence, all at UCSD and letter grade D or better. CCE 120 begins Fall 2025. CCE 1/2/3 are offered fall/winter/spring, with respectively fall/spring/winter identified as off-cycle terms with fewer seats. The page describes CCE120 using skills from CCE1–3 or transfer CCE110; it does not publish a complete formal prerequisite catalog.

requirements.title: Eighth breadth grading and overlap
requirements.summary: Two courses each in arts, humanities, natural sciences, quantitative methods/engineering and social sciences. D or better, or Pass; major/minor/university overlap permitted. Approved AP/IB/transfer credit applies. Humanities includes language at third-quarter level or higher, with listed 100–199 language ranges as open predicates. No IGETC waiver for first-year admits.

requirements.title: Eighth prior credit and open petitions
requirements.summary: California community-college courses taken before UCSD may satisfy equivalent breadth areas through their IGETC/CalGETC approvals. After starting UCSD, coursework must articulate to an approved UCSD course or receive a petition approval; petitions are not guaranteed. Off-list breadth courses are an open petition route, not a missing finite approved list.

requirements.title: Eighth current university rule summary
requirements.summary: Current page: 180 total/60 upper-division units; UC GPA at least 2.0; no more than 25% of UCSD units P/NP; 35 of final 45 units at UCSD; distance-designated courses below 50% unless the major is approved as a distance program. This residence figure agrees with Senate but differs from separately retained older college catalog wording. Climate applies to lower-division entrants from Fall2024. Eighth says F-1/J-1 students receive an AHI waiver at the end of the final quarter; retain the separate university petition language rather than assuming identical processing.

requirements.title: Eighth first-year quarter limit
requirements.summary: From Fall2019 first-year entrants have twelve quarters. Extra quarters require a completion plan approved by college and major. Summer, approved part-time quarters and quarters withdrawn from all courses do not count.

requirements.title: Eighth transfer CCE sequence
requirements.summary: Transfer sequence is CCE110 and120, four units each, both at UCSD for letter grade D or better. CCE110 begins Fall2026; both offered fall/winter/spring.

requirements.title: Eighth certified-transfer branch
requirements.summary: Complete IGETC/CalGETC before transfer and send separate official certification, or complete lower-division GE at a UC/four-year institution and provide official reciprocity. Lower-division breadth is waived; CCE110/120 remain. These agreements apply only to students admitted as transfers.

requirements.title: Eighth other-transfer branch
requirements.summary: Individual course review determines remaining first-year breadth. Complete CCE110/120, two additional college-level writing courses (often already completed before transfer), and all remaining GE not satisfied by prior courses/test scores. Pre-UCSD California community-college IGETC/CalGETC area approvals can meet equivalent breadth; later courses need UCSD equivalence or approved petition. Review begins mid-August and continues through fall; students receive their pathway determination.

requirements.title: Eighth transfer quarter limit
requirements.summary: From Fall2019 transfer entrants have six quarters, excluding summer, approved part-time terms and all-course withdrawals. Additional time requires a completion plan approved by major and college. Transfer students meet ELWR before enrollment; DEI remains required.

requirements.title: Seventh first-year Synthesis sequence
requirements.summary: SYN1 or1R, then SYN2 or2R, then SYN100; all at UCSD and letter graded. SYN1 requires Seventh membership and ELWR; SYN2 requires SYN1/1R; SYN100 requires Seventh membership, upper-division standing and completion of1/1R and2/2R. No credit for both normal and R version. SYN1/1R satisfies climate for lower-division entrants from Fall2024.

requirements.title: Seventh alternatives policy
requirements.summary: Two courses in each of five areas. Approved R variants, AP/IB and transfer credit apply; letter or P/NP grading, and major/minor/university overlap are permitted. Upper-division language is an open Humanities route with college advising; not every language course is separately enumerated.

requirements.title: Seventh High-Impact qualification
requirements.summary: One two-to-four-unit experiential course; may overlap major/minor/university requirements, letter or P/NP. The finite department pool retains petitions (MAE190,VIS108), CAT124 TEA request and EDS139 corequisite bundle. Any two-to-four-unit course numbered195–199 qualifies; no inventory of every such offering is implied.

requirements.title: Seventh approved experiential routes
requirements.summary: Any upper-division AIP internship, any two-to-four-unit EAP/OAP/Global Seminar course, or completion of California Ecology and Conservation can fulfill High-Impact. Other credit-bearing experiences require a petition. UCDC research seminar may count toward Alternatives by petition. These are open approved routes, not finite missing course lists.

requirements.title: Seventh current degree policy
requirements.summary: Current page:180 total/60 upper-division units, UC GPA at least2.0, no more than25% UCSD units P/NP, and35of final45units atUCSD. Its end-of-final-quarter F1/J1 AHI waiver wording is retained separately from the university petition wording.

requirements.title: Seventh IGETC/reciprocity transfer route
requirements.summary: All transfers complete SYN100 (four units, at UCSD and letter graded) plus one two-to-four-unit High-Impact course (letter/P-NP except SYN150 requires letter). Full pre-transfer IGETC certification or official UC/four-year reciprocity waives lower-division GE; documentation is required. This page names IGETC and does not independently establish CalGETC treatment; no inferred substitution.

requirements.title: Seventh partial or uncertified transfer route
requirements.summary: Partial IGETC may leave at most two requirements, completed at P or C− or better, plus SYN100 and High-Impact. Without an agreement, course-by-course review and petitions determine remaining GE after prior coursework/tests. Agreements apply only to students admitted as transfers.

requirements.title: Seventh transfer enrollment and optional preparation
requirements.summary: Transfers are stated to meet SYN100 prerequisites and receive preauthorization from winter of their first UCSD year. Optional SYN150/150R is transfer-only and must precede SYN100; it can satisfy High-Impact only for letter grade. No credit for both150and150R. It is recommended preparation, not an added mandatory course.

requirements.title: Revelle humanities substitution limits
requirements.summary: First-year entrants from Fall2017 take HUM1/2/3 and at least one of4/5 at UCSD; only one of4/5 can be an approved transfer substitution. Earlier first-year entrants through Fall2016 take1/2 and at least one of3/4/5 at UCSD, allowing up to two approved substitutions. Transfer entrants can fulfill HUM3–5 with three approved quarter courses, two semester courses, or one semester course plus one UCSD HUM3/4/5. This transfer-policy wording differs from the current transfer GE page choosing two of HUM3/4/5; preserve the discrepancy.

requirements.title: Revelle humanities transfer grading and review
requirements.summary: Letter grades required for UCSD and transferred humanities. Prior-to-matriculation philosophy/history/literature/humanities receives summer evaluation without petition. After UCSD enrollment use this approved list or petition with syllabus/course description; off-list approval is rare, not guaranteed. ASSIST listings alone are insufficient from Fall2017. Content duplication normally yields no additional units, though subject-credit review is possible.

requirements.title: Revelle humanities duplicate-content exceptions
requirements.summary: One course normally allowed from each Introduction and History list, subject to repetition rules. Foothill HUMN5and6 both count only without prior equivalent1400s-to-present credit. DeAnza HIST6B can accompany another listed course; both6B/6C can count only without prior History-category credit. CSU Dominguez Hills HUM200 was renumbered HUM204 in Fall2021 and only one can count. DeAnza/Foothill use quarters; others on these lists use semesters. No conversion or course units are inferred.
